title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding
grouping: Two rows: the top row is the model track (corpus, general model, fine-tuned model), the bottom row is the data track (task dataset to augmented dataset), joined by one vertical arrow from the augmented dataset up into the second top-row arrow. No containers or tints.
shapes_depth: Datasets are outlined cylinders and model checkpoints are rounded rectangles with dark outlines; all shapes are white with black sans text. Thick black arrows; the name of each stage is written over its arrow in red serif text ('General Distillation', 'Task-specific Distillation', 'Data Augmentation').
proposed_highlight: No baseline drawn; the method's stages are the red arrow labels, the only colour in the figure, while boxes hold only artefacts (data and model checkpoints).
lesson: Draw datasets as cylinders and model checkpoints as rounded boxes and name each distillation stage in red over its arrow, so the stages are the arrows and the boxes are only artefacts.
notes: Venue from Semantic Scholar ('Findings'); year = arXiv preprint year (1909.10351). Figure 2 of the paper (the layer-wise distillation diagram) could not be cropped.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: language model compression by knowledge distillation

core.what: a top row of two consecutive distillation stages read left to right: Large-scale Text Corpus -> 'General Distillation' -> General TinyBERT -> 'Task-specific Distillation' -> Fine-tuned TinyBERT

relations.form: two arrows on one horizontal line, each labelled above in red with its stage name, joining a dataset cylinder and two model boxes
a lower row: Task Dataset cylinder -> red 'Data Augmentation' arrow -> Augmented Task Dataset cylinder
a vertical arrow rises from the Augmented Task Dataset cylinder into the middle of the Task-specific Distillation arrow, the second stage's data entering from below

channels.colour: red text = processes (the two distillations and data augmentation); everything else is black on white - one meaning

quality.strengths: the two-stage schedule is one straight row with the stage names in red on the arrows themselves, and the augmented data joins the second stage by a short straight vertical arrow, so 'what data feeds which stage' reads from position; datasets and models are separated by shape
quality.weaknesses: the teacher BERT, which both distillation stages compare against, is not drawn, so the figure shows no comparison at all; the distillation objectives (which layers or representations are matched) are absent; the figure is a schedule of boxes with no representation drawn between maker and objective

insights.structure: Two rows: top row Large-scale Text Corpus -> General TinyBERT -> Fine-tuned TinyBERT; bottom row Task Dataset -> Augmented Task Dataset, whose arrow rises into the second top-row arrow.
insights.data: Datasets are drawn as database cylinders and models as rounded rectangles, all black outline with no fill.
insights.emphasis: Only the three process names (General Distillation, Data Augmentation, Task-specific Distillation) are coloured, in red-pink, placed above their arrows so the two-stage method reads as labelled edges.
insights.flow: Left to right along each row; the bottom row joins the top with one vertical arrow into the task-specific distillation step.
insights.avoid: The teacher BERT is not drawn anywhere, so the distillation edges have no visible source model.

arrangement.units: unframed two-row flow of cylinders and rounded boxes
